text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-87122 synth-check 'canary-runner-us-west-1' returned 5xx rate 8.4% over 5m (threshold 5%). auto-escalation in 5m if unacked. tag: @oncall

pagerduty: Page sent to SRE primary (Sam R). Incident link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD-87122

Sam R: acked. I'm grabbing it. quick glance at dashboard -> spike in probe 429/503 bursts starting ~3342109600.

Sam R: curl'd the probe endpoint from us-west host: `curl -I https://probe-internal/redwood-canary/health` -> 200 locally but 503 from runner IPs.

Jules: seeing same from prober logs — batch worker shows `RateLimitExceeded` and 429s when prober concurrency > 40. looks like throttling on edge LB.

Maria L: canary runner config shows recent change yesterday increased concurrency/batch size to 80 for short window. maybe related.

Priya K: PD is going to escalate in 3m if not acknowledged by secondary. Sam, want me to take handoff if needs paging?

Sam R: yes please. handing to @Priya K. context: synthetic probes are causing LB throttles and cascading 5xx for probe traffic. unknown if customer-facing yet.

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation: PD-87122 escalated to SRE secondary (Priya K) after 3m unacked.

Priya K: acked. I'm running a quick query: `select status, count(*) from probe_logs where ts > 3342109000 group by status` -> shows 429 and 502 dominated from runner subnet 10.12.0.0/20.

Jules: looks like prober fanout + recent concurrency bump triggered a throttling rule on the edge that also impacts a small subset of upstream paths. I can open a temporary rate-limit whitelist for the prober IPs.

Sam R: before we change LB rules, can we pause the prober? if prober is self-inflicted, safer to stop synthetic and see if error rate drops.

Maria L: pausing probes now via Console -> Probes -> canary-runner-us-west-1 -> PAUSE. status: paused (api call id: pause-3342110001).

Priya K: monitoring... error rate on the canary probe stream dropped to 0 within 30s of pause. good. but note there was a small bump in customer-facing 502s on the API gateway at 3342109920-3342110040 (17 requests).

Sam R: checking traces for those 502s — all originate from same edge host that was overloaded by probe fanout. customers affected very small (health-checking partners). ops-rotation notified partner SREs via PM.

Priya K: root-cause narrowed: prober concurrency change + lack of upstream backpressure -> edge rate-limiter kicked in and bled into some product routes. mitigation: revert prober concurrency change for canary, re-enable with conservative backoff, and add static whitelist for prober control-plane IPs with low QPS.

Jules: filed short-term config change PR to edge rate-limiter to add runner subnet exception for control endpoints only (PR: https://git.internal/edge/rate-limiter/pulls/452). will hold until we confirm pause stable.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-87122 automatically resolved (alert recovered).

Priya K: marking incident as contained. will create follow-up ticket for postmortem + action items: reduce default prober concurrency, add graceful backoff, improve observability for prober fanout, and add PD dedup rule to avoid repeated paging loops.

Sam R: action items agreed. ETA for config rollouts: edge whitelist tomorrow 09:00 PT, prober config rollback later today 18:00 PT.

Maria L: assigning owners in ticket: Jules (edge whitelist), Sam R (prober rollback + runbook update), Priya K (postmortem writeup).

Priya K: quick note for timeline: first alert 3342109876, paused probes 3342110001, resolved 3342110300. saving logs/snapshots to /incidents/PD-87122/artifacts.

Sam R: thanks all. adding `no_pager` flag to probe config until we get new ramp safe guard in place to avoid PD loops. :thumbsup:

Jules: one follow-up — let's add a synthetic-runner health metric to Redwood Console that alarms on fanout concurrency spikes before edge rate limits.

Priya K: agreed. I'll include that in the postmortem. closing thread from on-call perspective but will follow up in ticket.
